review_notes: I read the whole of Tail.lean and the definitions it depends on in Kernel.lean: parabolicRho₂, parabolicRieszKernel and parabolicRieszShell. I grepped for other uses of positiveShell, parabolicTailKernelConstant and parabolicRieszShell, and found none outside Tail.lean for positiveShell and parabolicTailKernelConstant. The file has no @[simp] declarations of its own. The only simp-interface weakness I found is that positiveShell has no membership or unfolding lemma, so call sites unfold it with simpa. I could not run Lean, so I don't know whether the suggested lemma would fire in every spot. Other simpa calls in the file (such as the `mul_comm` and `mul_left_comm` ones) are local proof style rather than interface problems, so I did not report them.

findings.excerpt:
def positiveShell (R : ℝ) (n : ℕ) (z : ParabolicPoint) : Set ParabolicPoint :=
  parabolicRieszShell R (n : ℤ) z
findings.problem: positiveShell is a plain def that only specializes parabolicRieszShell to a natural-number index. It has no rewrite lemma, so simp can neither expose its definition nor fold it back. Call sites therefore pass the constant itself to simp, as in `simpa [a, s, positiveShell] using hw.1` and `simpa [s, b, positiveShell] using positive_shell_cylinder_subset hR n z`. The helper `positive_shell_cylinder_subset` is stated for `parabolicRieszShell R (k : ℤ) z`, not for `positiveShell`. The goal and hypothesis therefore only match after simp unfolds the definition. `exists_positive_shell` has the same mismatch: it gives a `parabolicRieszShell` membership, and `positive_shell_cover` re-wraps it by defeq. In the other direction, simp can unfold `positiveShell` to `parabolicRieszShell R ↑n z`, but only when it is told to. Nothing gives a canonical form for `w ∈ positiveShell R n z`.
findings.proposed_change: Add a membership lemma such as `@[simp] theorem mem_positiveShell : w ∈ positiveShell R n z ↔ (2:ℝ)^(n:ℝ) * R ≤ parabolicRho₂ z w ∧ parabolicRho₂ z w < (2:ℝ)^((n:ℝ)+1) * R := Iff.rfl`. Alternatively, add `positiveShell_def : positiveShell R n z = parabolicRieszShell R (n:ℤ) z := rfl`. Use `positiveShell` directly in the statements of `positive_shell_cylinder_subset` and `exists_positive_shell`, so the `simpa [..., positiveShell]` unfoldings at lines 215 and 233 can become plain `hw.1` and `exact`. If the wrapper is purely an alias, a `@[reducible]` abbrev would achieve the same effect. The `Int.cast`/`Nat.cast` forms still need a simp lemma such as `Int.cast_natCast`, which simp already has.
findings.benefit: Readers and later files get a single canonical, loop-free normal form for shell membership. Unfolding this definition no longer needs ad hoc simp sets, and simpa calls no longer depend on definitional unfolding to match the lemma statements.
